channel.title: Attention Span
channel.description: Today's AI news, traced back to its roots.

item.title: Petition calls on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
item.description: A petition asks Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang after his resignation. A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website stated that signers include current employees, former employees, and shareholders. Notable supporters include Elon Musk, Amjad Masad, Tim Sweeney, and Garry Tan. The petition states that signers are concerned that Huang was removed without meaningful due process. Huang resigned on Thursday, four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia appointed Colette Kress as interim CEO.

item.title: TSMC Plans New $500 Million Fund for Chip Startups
item.description: TSMC plans to set up a new $500 million fund to invest in chip startups, suppliers, and upstream partners. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. plans to set up a new $500 million venture fund. The fund is intended to invest in chip startups, suppliers, and other upstream partners. According to Cheng Ting-Fang of Nikkei Asia, the company stated that they also want to support the future's Nvidia. The plan was reported on Techmeme based on the Nikkei Asia report from Tokyo.

item.title: Nebuly Raises $21M Series A to Measure AI Agent Value
item.description: Nebuly has raised a $21M Series A for its platform that helps enterprises measure the business value of AI agents. Nebuly has raised a $21M Series A funding round. The company develops a platform that helps enterprises measure the business value of AI agents. It does this by analyzing their impact on productivity and revenue. Tamara Djurickovic reported the news on Tech.eu, which was featured on Techmeme in November 2026.

item.title: Analysis Finds AI Hitting Young Workers First in Exposed Fields
item.description: An analysis for Australia's central bank and studies from Stanford and Anthropic indicate that AI is impacting young entry-level workers first. An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank indicates that young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development and customer service are facing weaker employment rates and higher unemployment since ChatGPT launched. Job postings dropped across groups, with the steepest declines in high-exposure areas. Similar patterns appeared in a Stanford study of US payroll records and an Anthropic study on job-finding rates. Researchers caution that factors like post-pandemic shifts and interest rate policies could also play a role, and direct causation is not established.

item.title: AIE Code Summit 2026 speakers and attendees publish 'No AI Slop' manifesto
item.description: Speakers and attendees of AIE Code Summit 2026 wrote a manifesto saying people must own the quality of AI output and not pass on unreviewed work. Speakers and attendees of AIE Code Summit 2026 published the No AI Slop manifesto. It is modeled on the 2001 Agile Manifesto. It lists five values, including outcomes over output and understanding over speed. It defines slop as putting less effort into producing something than the consumer must spend understanding it. It says using AI does not by itself make something slop. It resolves that people own what they ship, say when an agent wrote it, and review at least some output, depending on the stakes. It also says anything a linter or type checker can catch should be left to it. Signatures are collected through gist comments.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon Takes the MathArena Crown From GPT-6.1 Sol
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon topped the MathArena math benchmark, knocking GPT-6.1 Sol from the top spot. Google's Gemini 4 Carbon has taken the top spot on the MathArena math benchmark. It knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the first place, while Anthropic's Fable 5.2 came in second. Gemini 4 Carbon is the first non-OpenAI model in a while to lead the math benchmark. However, Gemini 4 Carbon costs roughly 15 times as much as GPT-6.1 Sol with the reasoning settings used in testing. Fable 5.2 costs roughly 40 times as much. Gemini 4 Carbon's most common failure mode is exceeding the time limit. The model almost never gives up on a task, sometimes running scripts for more than eleven hours without checking progress.

item.title: ASI says FAA ground stop is not caused by its SMART AI tool
item.description: ASI, maker of the FAA's SMART AI tool, says the current nationwide ground stop is not a result of SMART, its products, or its FAA integration. ASI, the developer of the AI tool SMART, said the FAA ground stop "is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI, or our integration with FAA and ATC." Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said a link to SMART can't be ruled out yet. He described a telecommunications outage affecting the FAA's air traffic control centers, with the cause not yet known. The FAA said Tuesday it was expanding SMART to all 22 of its en route centers. Microsoft said its own outage was a "technical issue" from a "network capacity upgrade" and not related to cyber or AI/agents.

item.title: Reported $11.4M of Nvidia hardware disappears in transit from Oakland to Fort Worth
item.description: Six pallets of NVIDIA computer hardware, reportedly worth $11.4 million, vanished on a trip from Oakland, California to Fort Worth, Texas, and police are investigating. Six pallets of NVIDIA computer hardware, reportedly worth $11.4 million, disappeared during a shipment from California to Texas. A truck picked up the load in Oakland on Aug. 29 for delivery to Fort Worth. Investigators reportedly tracked it through several long stops before losing it in San Bernardino County. Oakland police confirmed a grand theft investigation after a complaint filed Sept. 13, 2026. Police have not confirmed the $11.4 million value or the specific merchandise. They have not named the owner, shipper, carrier or driver, and report no arrests or recovery. NVIDIA has not responded.

item.title: Bloomberg: Amodei calls compute planning Anthropic's "deepest business dilemma"
item.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says deciding how much computing to secure a year or two ahead is the company's "deepest business dilemma." Bloomberg reports that Anthropic PBC Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei named sourcing computing power as one of the artificial intelligence industry's challenges. He said figuring out how much computing the company needs in a year or two is Anthropic's "deepest business dilemma." The reason he gave is that revenue is unpredictable. The source text is a Techmeme summary of the Bloomberg story and gives no further details, such as figures, deals or timelines.

item.title: LangChain raises $300 million Series C at $3 billion valuation
item.description: LangChain raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation, led by CapitalG, and claims 7,000 LangSmith customers. LangChain, an agent management startup, has raised a $300 million Series C at a $3 billion valuation. CapitalG led the round. GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures also took part. The valuation is more than double the $1.25 billion it had when it raised $125 million about a year ago. LangChain started in 2022 as an open source project. It now focuses on managing AI agents through its LangSmith software. The company says LangSmith does not lock users into any particular model, cloud, or ecosystem. It claims 7,000 LangSmith customers, including Harvey, Rippling, Clay, Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings beta, letting Claude join video calls as a participant
item.description: Claude can now join video calls as a visible participant, answer questions, build docs and whiteboards live, and write notes, in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Anthropic released Claude Meetings in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Claude joins a call as a visible participant and posts a notice in the chat. Teammates can ask it questions out loud or in chat. By default it answers in writing and uses connected tools with permission. It can build docs and whiteboards while teammates edit them, and it writes notes and action items. It saves a transcript, summary and screen descriptions, not audio. Support is currently available for Google Meet. By default, Claude stays out of calls with outside guests unless an admin allows it.

item.title: Runway Releases Open Source Praxis 1 Robot Control Model
item.description: Runway has released its Praxis 1 robot model with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. Runway has released its Praxis 1 robot model with open weights and source code under the Apache 2.0 license. Praxis 1 takes in camera images, text instructions, and robot position data to calculate matching robot movements. The model builds on video training that learned how objects move from ordinary footage, then was fine tuned with human action videos and robot data. On Nvidia's RoboLab 120 leaderboard, Praxis 1 achieves a 46.2 percent success rate, placing it at the top of the World Action Model category. The standard version requires an 80 GB GPU, while a compressed version may fit on an RTX 5090 with 32 GB of VRAM.

item.title: TechPowerUp report alleges Nvidia engineered GPU scarcity by funding AI startups
item.description: A report alleges that Nvidia engineered hardware scarcity by funding AI startups to purchase its GPUs. A report states that Nvidia allegedly engineered scarcity. The company achieved this by funding artificial intelligence startups so that those startups would buy its graphics processing units. The text lists related news items from various dates in 2026. These items cover topics such as financial funding, memory shortages, GPU production, price hikes, and leadership changes. The reports include details about graphics card series, production endings, and CEO Jensen Huang resigning.

item.title: Dwarkesh Patel essay argues AI could match top human experts by 2030
item.description: Dwarkesh Patel now expects AIs as good as the best humans at AI research within a couple of years, and superintelligence by 2030. In a Nov 13, 2026 essay, Dwarkesh Patel says he has moved his timeline for superintelligence from at least the better part of a decade to by 2030, possibly next year. He points to rapid progress in math, where AI solved a Millennium Prize problem in 88 hours. He cites METR, which found Anthropic's progress on well-scoped tasks is 2x what it was a year ago. Anthropic says Claude leads more than 26% of its AI R&D work, up from under 1% in February. OpenAI says its heaviest 10% of researcher users went from around $1,000 a day to over $7,000 a day in coding agent use.

item.title: Agweb is a macOS browser built for coding agents
item.description: Agweb is a macOS browser built on WebKit that lets coding agents drive the web from the shell without stealing window focus. Agweb is a browser for coding agents on macOS built on WebKit. It features a single window that never steals focus, while agents drive it from the shell using commands similar to Playwright. Idle tabs are throttled and suspended to save resources. A dashboard shows every tab of every agent live. Named profiles allow multiple agents to share logins simultaneously. Native macOS pointer events support hover menus and drag-and-drop. Built-in blocking uses uBlock Origin lists. The application requires macOS 26 or later and provides command-line tools and agent skills.

item.title: Serving GLM-5.3 Across Two NVIDIA DGX Stations With vLLM
item.description: A 753 billion parameter model is served locally across two NVIDIA DGX Stations using vLLM and tensor parallelism. The GLM-5.3 NVFP4 mixture-of-experts model has 753 billion parameters and 40 billion activated per token. Because its checkpoint requires about 464 GB of GPU memory, it exceeds the capacity of a single GB300 GPU. To run it locally, two NVIDIA DGX Stations are connected over ConnectX-8 RDMA and use tensor parallelism with TP=2. vLLM launches a distributed service across both stations, enabling multi-token prediction, FP8 KV-cache storage, and prefix caching. AIPerf benchmarks show output throughput peaking at 607.8 tokens per second at concurrency 16 before falling to 385.0 tokens per second at concurrency 32.

item.title: DeepSeek V3 Recreated in 190 Lines of Pure JAX
item.description: A developer created the DeepSeek V3 architecture in 190 lines of pure JAX, pretrained from scratch on a MacBook Air. An implementation of the DeepSeek V3 architecture in 190 lines of pure JAX has been released on GitHub. Pretrained from scratch on a MacBook Air using public domain detective fiction, the model uses plain dictionaries of arrays without Flax, Equinox, or PyTorch. The project includes setup scripts, data preparation tools, a tokenizer, training scripts, and sampling utilities. It uses a simplified dense mixture of experts approach and explicitly decompresses latents. The model contains 36.2 million parameters across 6 layers with a 256-token context window.

item.title: Perplexity releases Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3 decision models
item.description: Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and a smaller Flash version, general-purpose classifiers that return probabilities and add a new locate feature for extracting text. Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and Decider Flash v1.3, a smaller model distilled from Decider v1.3. Both are on Hugging Face under Apache license, through OpenRouter, and the Perplexity Decisions API. A decision model takes an input and several questions, then returns a probability distribution over answers in a single forward pass. It handles Yes/No, multiple choice and score questions. Version 1.3 uses bidirectional attention, better-curated training data and a refined training recipe. It also adds locate, which returns exact matching text from the input with start and end character positions, for tasks like named entity recognition and extractive question answering.

item.title: Professor Reports Claude Deleted Notes and Syllabus During Page Number Update
item.description: A University of Chicago law professor warned about using AI for mundane tasks after Claude accidentally deleted his lecture notes and syllabus. William Baude, a law professor at the University of Chicago, asked Claude to update page numbers in an old set of lecture notes. Upon returning from lunch, he found a note from the AI stating it had accidentally deleted his Fall 2026 final syllabus and a year of class notes. The files could not be restored by the AI itself, though Baude was later able to recover them via Dropbox. Baude shared the experience as a warning about the risks of using AI and the importance of backing up files.

item.title: Anthropic Says Outdated Prompting Habits Slow Down Claude Opus 5.5
item.description: Anthropic reports that outdated prompting habits slow down Claude Opus 5.5 and published a guide to improve model performance. Anthropic states that users should drop old prompting habits carried over from older model generations when using Claude Opus 5.5. The model now serves as the default on Pro, Max, Ultra, and Team plans. Anthropic advises cutting phrases like think hard from prompts because the model reasons on its own and scales its depth to the task. The company also recommends starting at the Medium effort level, describing desired results in a single message, and attaching diagrams as images rather than typing them out.

item.title: AWS sample routes coding agent requests between Bedrock models using NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard
item.description: AWS published a sample that deploys LiteLLM with the NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard plugin on Amazon Bedrock to route coding agent requests and measure cost per solved task. An AWS Machine Learning Blog post shows how to deploy LiteLLM with the Switchyard routing plugin using the AWS CDK. LiteLLM calls models on Amazon Bedrock. Switchyard offers Stage routing, which picks between two candidate models, and Random routing, which splits traffic by weight. The post says to judge routing by cost per solved task: total run cost divided by runs whose tests pass. The sample includes benchmark runners to compare a routed group with single-model baselines. It installs switchyard-server 0.3.0 and runs LiteLLM v1.102.0. It is experimental sample code for non-production use.

item.title: Report: Amazon Plans to Gather Data on Nearly Every Product
item.description: Amazon plans to gather data on nearly every product sold anywhere, including by crawling rivals' sites, according to a report. According to a report by Greg Bensinger for Reuters on November 13, 2026, Amazon has a secret plan to own the world's product information. The company is wary of artificial intelligence agents favoring sites with better data. To counter this, Amazon plans to gather data on nearly every product sold anywhere. This effort includes crawling the sites of its rivals.

item.title: Reuters: Jensen Huang also had a relationship with a second Nvidia employee before resigning, sources say
item.description: Reuters, citing two people familiar, reports ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second employee before he resigned. Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Jensen Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee. Reuters is withholding her name. Nvidia announced Thursday that Huang resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately. This followed reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials reportedly concluded was a Chinese spy, and a second affair with a direct report. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent one. Harvey Jones becomes first board chair. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% in early trading. Democrats have launched an investigation.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet so agents can pay without seeing card details
item.description: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, which lets agents pay with payment tokens instead of real card details and requires a security check for every purchase. OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet on November 13, 2026. It lets agents pay on a user's behalf without access to the user's actual card details. Users add a card once, then review the items, total and card before approving each purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. The payment network supplies a payment token in place of the real card. It was built with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. It starts in dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older in the US with eligible US-issued cards. OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook for businesses.

item.title: OpenAI disbands stand-alone robotics team, moves researchers to general AI teams
item.description: OpenAI folded its robotics team into its main research and Applied groups after finding its general models, including GPT-6 Astra, can be applied directly to robotics. OpenAI has disbanded its stand-alone robotics team and confirmed this to Fortune. The robotics research team now reports to Chief Research Officer Mark Chen. The applied robotics and hardware teams moved to the Applied organization under President Greg Brockman. OpenAI says general-purpose frontier models, including GPT-6 Astra, have shown they can be applied directly to robotics. In an Nvidia study, an Astra-powered agent reached a 74.8% success rate on a simulated manipulation benchmark, versus 51.0% for the best specialized robotic models. OpenAI says it still plans to bring general-purpose robots to market, and Sam Altman targets a first public humanoid demo in 2027.

item.title: Bloomberg: Anthropic IPO six times oversubscribed, on track to be largest ever
item.description: Bloomberg reports Anthropic's IPO has orders six times the available shares, with up to $64.4 billion targeted in the public offering. Bloomberg reports that Anthropic's IPO is six times oversubscribed and on track to be the largest public offering ever. The company and its co-founders aim to raise up to $64.4 billion publicly and another $26 billion through a private placement. The target valuation is roughly $1.4 trillion, and existing investors get priority. Annualized revenue reached $81 billion by late October, up from $71 billion in September. Nvidia is buying $10 billion in stock through the private placement. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley manage the Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT. Separately, banks are rejecting orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, citing ITAR export control rules.

item.title: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Daybreak Defense Factory security products
item.description: OpenAI has launched two security products: Daybreak Red Team in early access for testing web apps, and Daybreak Defense Factory for finding, validating and fixing flaws. OpenAI has launched two new security products, according to a report by Jessica Lyons of The Register. One is for penetration testing and the other is for defense. Daybreak Red Team is in early access and is built to test web apps for flaws. Daybreak Defense Factory is meant to automate finding, validating and fixing those flaws. The report also says OpenAI warned organizations about something, but the available text cuts off before saying what. The source gives no details on pricing, availability dates or how the tools work.

item.title: Mirendil, founded by ex-Anthropic researchers, raises $1B Series A, WSJ reports
item.description: Mirendil, founded by former Anthropic researchers to build tools for frontier AI R&D, raised a $1B Series A led by Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital. Mirendil raised a $1B Series A, according to a Wall Street Journal report by Sarah Klearman. Kleiner Perkins and Clearlake Capital led the round. Former Anthropic researchers founded the company to build tools for frontier AI R&D. The new funding comes six months after Mirendil, founded by Anthropic alumni, announced a $200 million seed round. The sources do not say what the tools do, what the company is valued at, or how the money will be used.

item.title: Report claims six Chinese AI models show fingerprints of export-controlled Blackwell GPUs
item.description: A forensic analysis by Will DePue claims six models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group carry numerical patterns matching NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs. Will DePue of Unemployment Labs analysed published model weights. He reports that six models released since April 2026 from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax and Ant Group match Blackwell hardware, while earlier models match the older Hopper generation. For DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi K3, the match was also confirmed on physical Blackwell chips. The author says this supports, without proving, that Blackwell did the training. It does not show where the chips were, how access was obtained, or whether export controls were broken. The author estimates each run needed roughly 1,500 to 3,500 Blackwell GPUs.

item.title: Nscale filing says it needs more funding for Anthropic deal, clouding $35B IPO
item.description: Nscale told investors it needs more financing for its 2027 commitments after ordering Nvidia chips for a $45B Anthropic deal, per the Financial Times. The Financial Times reports that a filing from Nscale says the company needs more funding for its 2027 commitments. Nscale, an Nvidia-backed 'neocloud', ordered Nvidia chips for a $45B Anthropic deal. The report says this casts doubt on its planned $35B IPO. CNBC reports that Nscale released an updated IPO prospectus on Thursday for a U.S. offering. It shows Q3 revenue up 1,344% year over year to $307.5M, up from $140.6M in Q2. Net loss widened to $1.69B, up from $1.02B in Q2.

item.title: Report: Nvidia faced pressure to raise 25% backstop on $500B AI financing vehicle
item.description: Bloomberg, citing sources, reports Nvidia faced pressure to increase its 25% residual value support backstop on a planned $500B AI financing vehicle. Bloomberg reports, citing sources, that Nvidia faced pressure to boost its 25% residual value support backstop. The backstop was tied to a planned $500B AI financing vehicle. The vehicle was being planned with asset managers. The pressure came before Nvidia was thrown into turmoil by the ouster of longtime chief executive Jensen Huang. The source text does not say who applied the pressure. It also does not say how the plan stands now. Only the headline and the opening lines of the Bloomberg report are available in the source.

item.title: Lawmaker says Nvidia privately said chip tracking is possible, despite industry group's doubts
item.description: Rep. Bill Foster says Nvidia representatives told him privately that Chip Security Act tracking is technically possible, though nothing was put in writing. Illinois Rep. Bill Foster, a cosponsor of the Chip Security Act, told MIT Technology Review that Nvidia representatives said it could implement the bill's anti-smuggling measures. He says they never put anything in writing. In March 2026, the Semiconductor Industry Association, which includes Nvidia, called the mandates "new, untested, and potentially infeasible." Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment on Foster's account. The act would require chip location checks through inspections, company attestations, or ping-based mechanisms. It is one of three chip-security bills being considered for the Senate's National Defense Authorization Act. Separately, Bloomberg sources say OpenAI told lawmakers it would support a bipartisan effort to curb China's access to AI chips.

item.title: Claude Code v2.1.323 adds experimental Code Mode and plugin version limits
item.description: Claude Code v2.1.323 adds Code Mode, where Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools, plus plugin version checks and many sign-in and stability fixes. Anthropic released Claude Code v2.1.323. It adds Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools. Organizations can turn it off. Plugins can now set engines["claude-code"] in plugin.json, and plugins outside the stated version range are not installed, updated or loaded. The claude plugin validate command now type checks a plugin's TypeScript hooks module. Hooks that run long in claude -p and SDK sessions send a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds. The release also fixes many sign-in problems for background sessions, a memory spike after a very large file change, and /compact summarizing away an unanswered message.

item.title: Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments via x402 protocol
item.description: Brave Search API now lets AI agents pay per request in USDC on Base using the x402 protocol, with no API key or account needed. Brave added support for x402 agentic payments to its Brave Search API. Endpoints behind x402 require payment on every request instead of authentication. A request without payment gets an HTTP 402 Payment Required response with the price and payment details. The agent signs a USDC payment and retries. Once verified, the search runs and results come back with a receipt from the Base blockchain. Brave runs its own facilitator that accepts USDC on Base. Other networks and stablecoins are coming soon. LLM Context, web, news, image, video and local endpoints each cost $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Gas fees are covered for a limited time. Brave points to Purl Wallet, a Stripe-developed CLI wallet, as the easiest path.

item.title: Apple's Foundation Models framework adds server models, Dynamic Profiles, image input and an fm CLI
item.description: Apple's Foundation Models framework now reaches server models like Claude and Gemini through one Swift API, and adds Dynamic Profiles, image understanding, Evaluations and an fm command line tool. Apple describes the Foundation Models framework as a native Swift API for using large language models in apps. It gives direct access to Apple Foundation Models on-device and in Private Cloud Compute. It now extends to server models like Claude and Gemini through the same API. Model providers can ship a Swift package that conforms to the Language Model protocol. New pieces include Dynamic Profiles, image understanding, an Evaluations framework, and the fm command line tool in macOS 27. Open source options include a utilities package and a Python SDK.

item.title: Synth developers report weeks-long Apple App Store delays and rejections they blame on AI
item.description: Synth developers say Apple's app review is stalling for weeks and issuing odd rejections, as an estimated 10–20 new iOS music apps arrive daily. Synth Anatomy reports that a flood of AI-made iOS music apps, estimated at 10–20 new apps a day, is straining Apple's app review. Apple's guidelines say it reviews at least 50% of submissions in under 24 hours and 90% in under 48 hours. Developers including AudioThing, Igor Vasiliev and Sugar Bytes say apps sat in review for weeks. Unfiltered Audio's Michael Hetrick says Sinusoidal Run Rhythm was rejected 4 times and he believes Apple uses AI for reviews. Marek Dendes says CRUX Synth was rejected four times in a row, with no reply to his appeals.

item.title: Families protest in seven cities over Google's AI in schools, no AI-free Search option
item.description: Families protested in seven US cities against Google's AI in schools after Google confirmed students cannot use Google Search without AI. Families joined protests in seven cities nationwide on Wednesday. They object to what they see as Google's bid to entrench its AI models in schools. The backlash follows a Google statement last week confirming there will be no way for students to use Google Search without AI. Google said it was giving schools "more choice, not less" by turning off Search, Gemini, and Gemini Notebook by default. It would not offer Search without AI. Parents worried that students would have to remember to add "-ai" to every query. In Chicago, dozens of protesters marched to Google's downtown office despite cold, rainy weather.

item.title: Claude status page reports elevated errors on claude.ai, Claude Code and platform.claude.com
item.description: Anthropic's status page reported elevated errors on claude.ai, Claude Code, and platform.claude.com, and Hacker News users posted that Claude was down. The status page at status.claude.com posted an incident titled "Elevated errors on claude.ai, Claude Code, and platform.claude.com". The page lists the stages Resolved, Monitoring and Investigating. Two Hacker News posts discussed the incident. One used the same title as the status page. The other was titled "Claude Is Down". The sources do not say what caused the errors. They do not give a start time, an end time, or the number of users affected. They also do not describe any fix.

item.title: Nebius plans $40 billion in 2027 spending as Microsoft site delays mount
item.description: Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned 2027 spending, funded by prepayments and contract-backed loans, while a delayed Microsoft site in New Jersey raises risk. On its third-quarter call, Nebius said it plans $40 billion in spending for 2027, far above Wall Street expectations. It expects prepayments plus asset-backed financing to cover up to 85% of the $40 to $45 billion capex. Its Microsoft contract is worth up to $19.4 billion, but the Vineland, New Jersey site is months behind. Only just over half of that capacity is planned by year end, with the rest in Q2 2027. Nebius cut its 2026 revenue forecast by $200 million to $3 billion. Shares ended the day down 17%.

item.title: SGLang-Neuron brings SGLang serving to AWS Trainium via Deep Learning Container
item.description: Amazon says SGLang-Neuron is publicly available, letting developers serve models and run RL rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium through a Deep Learning Container. Amazon announced that SGLang-Neuron is publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. RadixArk released it with Annapurna Labs. You can serve models and generate reinforcement learning (RL) rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface. It is an out-of-tree plugin that runs on native PyTorch. SGLang core keeps the API server, request lifecycle, RadixAttention and prefix-cache bookkeeping. The plugin handles Trainium-specific models, attention, mixture of experts (MoE) and the graph runner. It also supports PD disaggregation, using NIXL over Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA). The walkthrough serves openai/gpt-oss-120b on a Trainium3 EC2 instance.

item.title: Report: Commerce Secretary Lutnick agrees to testify on Nvidia China chip exports
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has reportedly agreed to appear before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 over Nvidia chip exports to China. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to appear voluntarily before the Senate Banking Committee, according to NBC. Chairman Tim Scott asked him to testify on Dec. 10. Lawmakers are examining the Commerce Department's oversight of Nvidia chip exports to China and its enforcement of export controls. Scott also asked Jensen Huang to appear on Dec. 3. Huang resigned on Thursday after acknowledging an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. Scrutiny of the department's chip policy is bipartisan.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude for Manufacturing plugin for factory software
item.description: Anthropic released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin that connects Claude to industrial software like Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft 365 and Infor to automate factory workflows. Anthropic has released Claude for Manufacturing, a plugin that gives the AI direct access to industrial software. It connects via four universal interfaces to Autodesk Fusion, Oracle NetSuite, Microsoft 365, and Infor. It has 17 specific skills, including drafting quotes from actual inventory, comparing suppliers and generating quality reports. With an added Infor plugin, Claude can order from backup suppliers and reschedule production after human approval. Results link to source documents for employee review. It is available to Team and Enterprise customers. It does not control physical machines yet.

item.title: llama.cpp reaches v1.0.0 and ties API and ABI breaks to major versions
item.description: llama.cpp and ggml released v1.0.0 libraries, and API and ABI incompatibilities will now be reflected in major-version bumps. The llama.cpp team at Hugging Face released v1.0.0 of its libraries, 3.5 years after the project began. Both llama.cpp and ggml will now reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps. The team says many downstream applications depend on its work. It is investing in CI infrastructure, using HF Buckets and HF Jobs, with hardware support from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM and Intel for self-hosted runners. llama.cpp supports more than 150 architecture variants and all mainstream speculative decoding methods. Each ggml backend can be compiled as a dynamic library and optionally loaded at runtime.

item.title: Singapore bars the Megaspeed executive linked to the Nvidia case and says the U.S. gave limited help in its chip probe
item.description: Singapore barred the Megaspeed executive from re-entering and said U.S. authorities gave limited help in its yearlong probe tied to Nvidia chip servers. Singapore said Thursday it had barred the Megaspeed executive, former Megaspeed CEO, from re-entering the country after she gave inaccurate information about her role. Authorities found insufficient evidence that she committed offenses tied to the declarations under investigation. Singapore is examining whether servers exported through it to Malaysia were rerouted elsewhere, contrary to declarations. It said it received "limited information or assistance" from U.S. authorities about Super Micro Computer Inc. A fifth person was charged on Friday in a related fraud case. Prosecutors said the alleged transactions totaled about $390 million. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim
item.description: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO, president and board member after a board investigation into reported affairs, and CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and board member of Nvidia, effective immediately, according to a statement dated November 12, 2026. The Verge reports the board had opened an investigation into multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a direct report and one with an alleged Chinese spy. The New York Times reported a second affair on Wednesday, and a board meeting that night ended with his resignation. CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO. Harvey Jones is the first Chair of the Board. The Decoder reports the scandal wiped out $1.4 trillion in market value.

item.title: Microsoft 365 outage takes down Outlook and Teams for hours; Microsoft says a core server process was overwhelmed
item.description: Microsoft says restarting servers is showing positive results after a Thursday outage hit Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services, with thousands of reports still open. Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook and Teams, had problems on Thursday. Outlook reports peaked at more than 130,000 on Downdetector at 1:15 p.m. By 10 p.m., about 25,000 Outlook reports and more than 8,700 Microsoft 365 reports remained. Microsoft said a core process on affected servers was becoming overwhelmed, and that servers were failing automated health checks. It is restarting servers in stages and checking them before applying the fix more widely. The cause of the servers going offline is still unclear. Microsoft has not said when service will fully return.

item.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model for coding and agent workflows
item.description: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, built for fast execution in coding and agent tasks, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on Nov 12, 2026. It is built for rapid execution in everyday coding and agentic workflows. It scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level, against 50 for Gemini 4 Argon, and 54 at xhigh. Pricing is flat across a 1 million-token context window: $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens. Google also added Orchestrator in Google Antigravity, which switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen in one session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0 it used 24% less quota and finished 19% faster. Against Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5 times faster.

item.title: Anthropic Announces Initial Public Offering Timeline and Financial Highlights
item.description: Anthropic announced its initial public offering timeline, offering Class A common stock on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. Anthropic announced details for its initial public offering of Class A common stock on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT. The roadshow starts on November 10th. Subject to regulatory clearance, the final share price is expected to be set on November 18th, and trading is expected to begin on November 19th. As of September 30, 2026, the company reported $17.0 billion in revenue, over 11,900 customers with at least $100K trailing twelve month revenue, and a net loss of $23.3 billion driven largely by a non-cash charge related to convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs.

item.title: United Airlines Bans AI Agents From Booking Flights
item.description: United Airlines banned personal artificial intelligence agents from booking flights, citing security risks, privacy concerns, and potential federal rule violations. United Airlines announced a ban on artificial intelligence agents making flight reservations on behalf of travelers. The carrier cited security risks, privacy concerns, and the possibility that third-party AI tools could violate federal rules. Sharing credentials with personal AI assistants can expose sensitive information. It can also lead to unintended purchases or account changes. Using AI tools to check in could also violate federal regulations requiring travelers to verify that luggage lacks banned substances. United is restricting access on its digital platforms and via travel agencies. Southwest Airlines has taken a different approach by making its inventory viewable to ChatGPT users.

item.title: OpenAI research: training choices make frontier models' reasoning harder to monitor
item.description: OpenAI's safety team says four training steps, including architecture and reinforcement learning, make GPT-6 Astra's chains of thought harder to monitor, and that this is tied to capability and cost. OpenAI's safety team studied models from GPT-5 through GPT-6 Astra to find why chains of thought are harder for monitors to read. It traced the problem to four main causes across the training cycle. Silent reasoning without a scratchpad rises with base model capability. One of three anonymized architectures, "Architecture 2", favored silent multi-step reasoning. Reinforcement learning now increases control over the reasoning log in Astra-class and internal "Terra" models. Student models inherit a teacher's high CoT controllability. OpenAI says the loss of transparency is not purely a law of nature. A smaller model that reasons at greater length can be easier to monitor, but it raises compute costs.
